title: Wendell and the Choir
premise: Jude Eastwick, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics he carves, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things. When a dying courier presses a map of the king's own bones into his hands, Jude learns that the crown has been hollowed out and worn by a choir of bound spirits that feeds on royal memory. Hunted by the Guild's enforcers and guided by the dead themselves, Jude gathers a found family of outcasts — a disgraced choir-singer, a thief who can walk through grief, and the king's forgotten sister — to reach the crypt beneath the palace. In the end Jude must choose between unbinding the choir and letting it devour him, and he does both: he sings himself into the crown's place long enough for the true king to die free, then walks out hollow-voiced but alive, carrying justice no law would ever have granted.
about_author: Vesper Kavanagh is the pen name of a former cathedral archivist who spent a decade cataloguing funeral music before turning to fiction. They write from a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule and the church bells are slightly out of tune.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Jude Eastwick carves a relic bone while the dead whisper through it, balancing the Vellum Guild's ledgers. His POV establishes his careful, transactional loneliness and his gift: he hears whoever died holding the bone. Beat: quiet dread as one ledger entry refuses to balance.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: A dying courier collapses into Jude's workshop, pressing a rolled map into his hands — drawn on vellum made from a king's skin, charting the royal skeleton itself. The courier dies naming 'the choir.' POV Jude; beat: terror as Guild bells begin tolling an alarm he's never heard before.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Corvane summons Jude, all silk and threat, asking after a missing courier. Jude lies for the first time in his life. POV Jude; beat: the sick thrill and horror of deception, realizing the Guild trades in people, not just impossibilities.

chapters.title: The Singer Who Fell
chapters.summary: Jude seeks Sera Ilvane, a court soprano exiled for refusing to sing at the king's coronation renewal. She recognizes the map's notation as choral binding-marks. POV shifts to Sera; beat: her bitter hope that someone finally believes what she saw from inside the palace.

chapters.title: Thief of Grief
chapters.summary: To cross the city's warded gates they need Doss, a thief who slips through mourning crowds unnoticed because he carries others' grief like a cloak. POV Doss; beat: wary humor masking his fear that if he stops moving, his own buried grief will catch him.

chapters.title: The King's Forgotten Sister
chapters.summary: In a convent outside the walls lives Princess Maren, erased from records twenty years ago when her brother was crowned. She confirms the coronation date changed — moved to a night with no witnesses. POV Maren; beat: rage crystallizing into purpose after decades of being told she imagined everything.

chapters.title: Enforcers at the Bonehouse
chapters.summary: Guild enforcers raze Jude's workshop hunting the map. He escapes through the bone-cellars hearing the dead guide him — literally — via carved relics along the walls. POV Jude; beat: grief for his old life burning into resolve; the found family coalesces around shared loss.

chapters.title: Reading the Royal Bones
chapters.summary: Sera deciphers the map: each vertebra marked with a name — twelve singers bound into the crown, their voices sustaining the choir that wears the king. POV Sera; beat: horror and recognition — she knew two of the names, fellow students who 'died' before her exile.

chapters.title: The Road Through Hollowmere
chapters.summary: The company travels toward the capital through Hollowmere, a village where everyone smiles identically — a trial run of the choir's technique on commoners. POV Doss; beat: creeping wrongness; Doss absorbs the village's stolen joy and nearly drowns in it.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane intercepts them, offering Jude partnership: help the Guild control the choir rather than destroy it, and live richly. Jude refuses; a fight scatters the group. POV Jude; beat: temptation genuinely considered — power offered to the powerless — before refusal hardens him.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Regrouping in ruins, Maren admits she once heard her brother crying for help through a palace wall and did nothing, believing herself mad. POV Maren; beat: shame transmuted into fierce commitment; the group becomes family through confessed weakness.

chapters.title: The Twelfth Name
chapters.summary: Sera discovers the twelfth binding-name on the map is blank — reserved for a new voice. The choir needs a replacement; that's why the Guild hunts Jude, whose gift makes him the perfect candidate. POV Sera; beat: protective panic; the stakes turn personal.

chapters.title: Into the Undercity
chapters.summary: Doss leads them through the capital's undercity, past grief-clogged tunnels where the dead of old purges linger. The dead recognize Jude's gift and part for him. POV Doss; beat: awe and jealousy — everyone's ghosts answer Jude, never his own.

chapters.title: The Palace of One Voice
chapters.summary: Infiltrating the palace during a state banquet, they witness the king address the court in perfect unison with a hundred servants — the choir's harmony leaking outward. POV Maren; beat: heartbreak seeing her brother's face puppeted by something patient and hungry.

chapters.title: Captured
chapters.summary: Corvane betrays their location; enforcers take Sera and Doss. Jude and Maren escape into the crypts, but Jude hears Sera's voice already being rehearsed into the twelfth chair. POV Jude; beat: guilt and desperation; time collapses — the binding happens at dawn.

chapters.title: The Crypt Beneath the Crown
chapters.summary: Jude and Maren descend through the royal ossuary, the map guiding them bone by bone. The dead kings whisper warnings: the choir was meant as mercy, a way to keep good kings ruling past death. POV Jude; beat: moral vertigo — the corruption began as love.

chapters.title: Twelve Chairs
chapters.summary: They reach the crown-chamber: twelve thrones of bone, eleven occupied by translucent singers, a twelfth empty beside the enthroned thing wearing the king. Sera resists singing; Doss works loose. POV Sera; beat: defiance under pressure as she stalls with wrong notes.

chapters.title: The Choir Unmasked
chapters.summary: Jude uses a carved relic of the founder-king to force the choir to speak plainly: it devours royal memory to stay coherent, and the current king has almost nothing left. POV Jude; beat: cold clarity — this isn't possession to cure but a parasite to starve.

chapters.title: Dawn Binding
chapters.summary: Climax begins: enforcers flood the chamber, Corvane orders Jude bound to the twelfth chair. Maren fights to reach her brother; Doss unleashes every grief he's carried as a weapon against the enforcers. POV rotating; beat: chaos, sacrifice, the family holding the line.

chapters.title: The Twenty-First Verse
chapters.summary: Jude sits in the twelfth chair willingly and sings counterpoint, unraveling the choir's harmony from within while the dead kings lend him their voices. The crown cracks; the true king wakes, dying but himself. POV Jude; beat: transcendence through self-sacrifice — justice sung, not legislated.

chapters.title: After the Music
chapters.summary: The choir dissolves; Corvane flees into the Guild's collapse as its ledgers burn. Maren holds her brother as he dies free, naming her heir. Jude survives, voice rasped to a whisper, unable to hear the dead anymore. POV Maren; beat: grief braided with relief and inheritance.

chapters.title: A New Ledger
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Jude opens a modest workshop with Sera, Doss, and Maren as regulars — a found family keeping honest accounts. He cannot hear the dead, but sometimes, carving, he feels listened to. POV Jude; beat: earned peace, with a faint door left open for wonder.
